round: # The caption (show_en) is one short sentence to read along. The right choice is not always the first.
# Story 10: Mina goes to the bazaar (a girl tells it; the shopkeeper has the man's voice). Language up to unit 10.

say_en: f: Hello! My name is Mina. My mother wants tomatoes and eggs. I have a basket and some money.
show_en: My mother wants tomatoes and eggs.

say_en: f: This is the bazaar. It is big! Look at the shops.
show_en: This is the bazaar. It is big!

say_en: f: I want to buy tomatoes. Point to the tomatoes.
wrong_say_fa: این بادنجان رومی نیست. دوباره ببین و بادنجان رومی را نشان بده.

say_en: f: Hello! How much are the tomatoes? // m: Hello! They are forty afghani a kilo. They are fresh.
f: One kilo of tomatoes, please. // m: Here you are. // f: How much is one kilo of tomatoes?
wrong_say_fa: نه. دوباره گوش کن. یک کیلو بادنجان رومی چهل افغانی است.

say_en: f: I want eggs. // m: How many eggs do you want? // f: Six eggs, please.
show_en: How many eggs do you want?

say_en: f: Count six eggs for Mina.
wrong_say_fa: دوباره حساب کن. مینا شش تخم مرغ می‌خواهد.

say_en: f: How much is it? // m: It is seventy afghani. // f: Here is one hundred afghani. // m: Here is your change. Thirty afghani.
f: Thank you! Goodbye! // m: Goodbye, Mina! // f: Look, mother! Fresh tomatoes and six eggs. My mother is happy.

round: # Story 15: Hamid sells eggs (a boy tells it
picture: man's voice; his customer and the questions have the woman's voice). Language up to unit 15.

say_en: m: Good morning! My name is Hamid. This is my cart. I sell eggs and cheese at the bazaar.
show_en: I sell eggs and cheese at the bazaar.

say_en: f: Good morning! Do you have any eggs? // m: Yes, I have some. They are fresh. How many do you want? // f: Ten eggs, please.
f: Count ten eggs for the customer.
wrong_say_fa: دوباره حساب کن. مشتری ده تخم مرغ می‌خواهد.

say_en: f: Do you have any milk? // m: No, I don't have any milk. Sorry. I have some cheese. // f: Good. Half a kilo of cheese, please.
show_en: I don't have any milk. I have some cheese.

say_en: f: Hamid does not have any milk. What does he have?
wrong_say_fa: نه. حمید شیر و ماست ندارد. او کمی پنیر دارد. دوباره انتخاب کن.

say_en: f: How much is it? // m: The eggs are one hundred afghani and the cheese is fifty afghani. It is one hundred and fifty afghani.
show_en: It is one hundred and fifty afghani.
wrong_say_fa: نه. دوباره گوش کن. یکصد و پنجاه افغانی می‌شود.

say_en: f: Here is the money. Oh! My basket is heavy. I can't carry it. Can you help me? // m: Yes, I can!
show_en: Can you help me? Yes, I can!

say_en: f: Thank you, Hamid. You are a good boy. // m: Thank you. Goodbye!

round: # Story 20: A scarf for grandmother (a girl tells it; the shopkeeper has the man's voice). Language of the whole level.

say_en: f: Hello! I am Roya. This is my brother, Navid. We want to buy a scarf for our grandmother. We have three hundred afghani.
show_en: We want to buy a scarf for our grandmother.

say_en: f: Excuse me. Do you have any scarves? // m: Yes, I have some. Look! A red scarf and a blue scarf.
f: How much is the blue scarf? // m: It is five hundred afghani. // f: That is too expensive! How much is the red scarf? // m: It is three hundred and fifty afghani.
show_en: The blue scarf is too expensive!

say_en: f: Which scarf is cheaper?
wrong_say_fa: نه. چادر آبی پنجصد افغانی است. چادر سرخ سه‌صد و پنجاه افغانی است. کدام یک ارزانتر است؟

say_en: f: We have three hundred afghani. Can you make it cheaper, please? // m: All right. Three hundred afghani.
show_en: Can you make it cheaper, please?

say_en: f: How much do Roya and Navid pay?
wrong_say_fa: نه. دوباره گوش کن. دکاندار قیمت را ارزانتر کرد: سه‌صد افغانی.

say_en: f: Here is three hundred afghani. // m: Here is your scarf. // f: What do Roya and Navid say now?
wrong_say_fa: نه. وقتی کسی چیزی به ما می‌دهد، می‌گوییم تشکر. دوباره انتخاب کن.

say_en: f: Thank you very much! // m: You're welcome. Goodbye!
f: Grandmother, this scarf is for you! Grandmother is happy. She likes the red scarf. Goodbye!
